scenes.title: Father Wolf Wakes at Dusk
scenes.summary: Father Wolf wakes at the cave mouth on a warm evening while Mother Wolf lies with her four cubs, and Tabaqui the jackal appears at the threshold with flattering good wishes.

scenes.title: Tabaqui at the Cave
scenes.summary: Tabaqui enters despite being despised and feared for his mischief and madness, eats a dry bone, and deliberately unsettles Mother and Father Wolf by unluckily praising the cubs.

scenes.title: News of Shere Khan
scenes.summary: Tabaqui brings news Shere Khan has shifted hunting grounds; the wolves angrily discuss the lame tiger, hear his hunting whine, and recall the Law forbidding man-eating.

scenes.title: Shere Khan Burns His Feet
scenes.summary: Shere Khan's charge ends in an untigerish howl. Father Wolf hears him tumbling in the scrub, having jumped at a woodcutters' campfire and burned his feet, with Tabaqui with him. As something comes uphill through the thicket, Father Wolf crouches for his leap but checks himself in mid-spring.

scenes.title: A Man's Cub Among the Cubs
scenes.summary: A naked brown baby who can just walk stands holding a low branch and laughs up into Father Wolf's face. Father Wolf mouths him gently without scratching the skin and lays him among the cubs. Mother Wolf marvels at how little, naked, and bold he is as he pushes in for warmth, and Father Wolf marvels that he looks up without fear.

scenes.title: Shere Khan Demands His Quarry
scenes.summary: Shere Khan blocks the cave mouth with Tabaqui behind him and demands the man's cub, but Father Wolf angrily receives him, knowing the burnt tiger cannot force his way inside.

scenes.title: Raksha Claims Mowgli
scenes.summary: Father Wolf claims the cub for the free Wolves, and Mother Wolf as Raksha springs forward to defy and drive off Shere Khan, then keeps the fearless child and names him Mowgli the Frog.

scenes.title: Summoned to the Pack Council
scenes.summary: The Law requires cubs be shown to the Pack; Father Wolf waits, then brings Mowgli to the moonlit Council Rock for inspection.

scenes.title: Bought for a Bull
scenes.summary: Shere Khan claims Mowgli, none speak for him until Baloo offers teaching and Bagheera buys his life with a bull, winning the Pack's acceptance.

scenes.title: Entered into the Pack
scenes.summary: With Shere Khan roaring in defeat, Bagheera prophesies Mowgli will hunt him, and Akela orders Mowgli trained as one of the Free People.

scenes.title: Mowgli Learns the Jungle
scenes.summary: Ten years pass as Mowgli grows up with the wolf cubs, learning jungle lore, senses, swimming, and honey-hunting from Father Wolf, Baloo, and Bagheera.

scenes.title: The Law of the Bull
scenes.summary: Mowgli learns to climb and stare down wolves at Council, helps friends with thorns, distrusts men after seeing a trap, and learns from Bagheera never to kill cattle.

scenes.title: Shere Khan Courts the Young Wolves
scenes.summary: As Mowgli grows strong and forgets warnings about Shere Khan, Akela weakens and Shere Khan flatters discontented young wolves against him, while Bagheera warns Mowgli of danger.

scenes.title: Bagheera's Warning
scenes.summary: Bagheera warns Mowgli of the coming leadership challenge, reveals his own captive past and collar mark, and urges him to fetch the Red Flower of fire.

scenes.title: Akela Misses His Kill
scenes.summary: Mowgli runs back through the forest and hears the Pack hunting below. Akela springs at the Sambhur and misses, and Mowgli flees on to the village fields, where he hides by a hut and watches a woman and child tend fire on the hearth.

scenes.title: Stealing Fire from Men
scenes.summary: Mowgli seizes the boy's pot of red coals and feeds it with twigs to keep it alive. Climbing back, he meets Bagheera, learns the Pack sought to kill Akela and him, and shows the fire, remembering lying beside the Red Flower as a man's cub.

scenes.title: The Council Turns
scenes.summary: At the Council Rock with leadership open, Shere Khan and his wolves demand Mowgli while Akela and Bagheera defend the Law and the Pack's honor.

scenes.title: Master of Fire
scenes.summary: Mowgli rises with fire, declares himself Man, scatters the cowering wolves, beats Shere Khan, and frees Akela from death.

scenes.title: Farewell to the Cave
scenes.summary: Weeping human tears for the first time, Mowgli bids farewell to Mother and Father Wolf and his brothers, vowing to return with Shere Khan's hide.

scenes.title: Hunting-Song of the Seeonee
scenes.summary: The Hunting-Song of the Seeonee Pack closes the chapter with dawn, bell, track, and pack cry.

scenes.title: Lessons in the Law
scenes.summary: Baloo teaches Mowgli the Law of the Jungle while Bagheera watches. Their affectionate debate about beating and protecting the man-cub establishes tutelage and care.

scenes.title: The Master Words
scenes.summary: Mowgli is called to recite the Master Words for Hunting People, Birds, and Snakes. His success proves Hathi's gift protects him from all but his own tribe.

scenes.title: Warning Against the Bandar-log
scenes.summary: Mowgli boasts he will lead the Bandar-log. Baloo and Bagheera angrily warn him the Monkey People have no Law, no leaders, and are forbidden, as monkeys shower filth from above.

scenes.title: The Bandar-log Take Mowgli
scenes.summary: The Bandar-log, admiring Mowgli's stick huts and wanting him to teach them, follow him, Baloo and Bagheera to the midday nap and seize the sleeping Mowgli despite Baloo's alarm and Bagheera's charge.

scenes.title: Flight Along the Tree-Roads
scenes.summary: Carried under the arms by strong monkeys, Mowgli is swept prisoner along the high tree-roads in a wild, sickening rush of bounds, swings and drops above the jungle.

scenes.title: Message by Kite
scenes.summary: Mid-flight Mowgli spots Rann the Kite and gives the bird Master Word, begging him to mark his trail and tell Baloo and Bagheera where he is taken.

scenes.title: Seeking Kaa
scenes.summary: Baloo and Bagheera rage and grieve at their helplessness against tree-dwellers. Baloo remembers the Bandar-log fear only Kaa the Rock Python, and they go to seek him sleeping in new skin.

scenes.title: Bargaining with the Python
scenes.summary: Baloo and Bagheera flatter hungry, deaf Kaa and provoke him with the monkeys' insults. Kaa learns they hunt the Bandar-log for stealing their beloved man-cub.

scenes.title: Rann Brings Word
scenes.summary: Rann the Kite finds Baloo at dusk and reports that the Bandar-log have carried Mowgli beyond the river to the Cold Lairs.

scenes.title: Race to the Cold Lairs
scenes.summary: Bagheera and Kaa set out at full speed for the half-night journey to the Cold Lairs, leaving Baloo struggling to follow while they race side by side.

scenes.title: The Monkey City
scenes.summary: In the ruined Lost City, the monkeys vaunt themselves, force Mowgli to weave, and leave him hungry and disgusted as moonlight falls on the marble summerhouse terrace.

scenes.title: Bagheera and Kaa Wait for the Cloud
scenes.summary: Bagheera and Kaa watch the cloud from the ditch below the wall, knowing the Monkey People only fight at hundred-to-one odds. Kaa will take the west wall with the slope in his favor, while Bagheera will rush the terrace when the cloud covers the moon where the monkeys hold council over Mowgli.

scenes.title: Overwhelmed on the Terrace
scenes.summary: Under the cloud-covered moon Bagheera storms the terrace and strikes through rings of monkeys until numbers overwhelm him. The monkeys drop Mowgli through the broken dome into a cobra den where he gives the Snake's Call for protection, while Bagheera fights for his life toward the water-tanks and Baloo arrives bellowing to battle his way up the terrace as Kaa finally tops the west wall.

scenes.title: Kaa Attacks
scenes.summary: Kaa rushes straight into battle and strikes with full python force, knocking the monkeys away from Baloo in silence and scattering the crowd in terror at his name.

scenes.title: Kaa Frees Mowgli
scenes.summary: Feared as the night-thief, Kaa hisses the city into silence, halts the far-off reinforcements, and smashes the marble screen to free Mowgli from the cobras' trap.

scenes.title: Rescue and Thanks
scenes.summary: Bruised and bleeding, the reunited friends embrace. Mowgli courteously thanks Kaa in Jungle custom, pledging his kill and future help, and Kaa bids them leave before moonset.

scenes.title: The Hunger Dance
scenes.summary: Kaa begins the Hunger Dance, fascinating monkeys, bear, and panther alike. Only Mowgli's hands on their shoulders break the spell, letting the three slip to the jungle.

scenes.title: Rebuke After Kaa
scenes.summary: Shaken by Kaa's Hunger-Dance, Baloo and Bagheera rebuke Mowgli for playing with the Bandar-log, telling him it cost them wounds, time, and honor.

scenes.title: Punishment Settles Scores
scenes.summary: Mowgli accepts his fault under Jungle Law, Bagheera gives him love-taps that settle the score, then carries the sleeping boy home to Mother Wolf.

scenes.title: Road-Song of the Bandar-Log
scenes.summary: The Bandar-log sing their boastful Road-Song, prancing, dreaming, and jabbering like men but achieving nothing, revealing their vain and mindless nature.

scenes.title: Flight to the Distant Plain
scenes.summary: A death-song sounds as Mowgli flees his enemies at the Council, jogs nearly twenty miles down the valley to an unknown plain, and reaches a new village where herd-boys flee and pariah dogs bark at the thorn gate.

scenes.title: Begging Food at the Thorn Gate
scenes.summary: Hungry Mowgli sits by the gate and silently begs food, prompting a staring man to fetch the priest and a crowd of a hundred villagers, whom Mowgli regards as mannerless and meets with a frown.

scenes.title: Claimed as Nathoo
scenes.summary: Marked by wolf-bites, Mowgli is declared by the priest to be Messua's lost son Nathoo and taken to her hut, where he eats, is claimed as a son, and resolves to learn men's talk.

scenes.title: Mowgli Learns Man Speech
scenes.summary: Mowgli uses his jungle mimicry to repeat Messua's words almost perfectly and learns many hut names before dark, but refuses to sleep inside what feels like a panther-trap and climbs out the window, which Messua's husband accepts.

scenes.title: Night Visit of Gray Brother
scenes.summary: Sleeping in the grass outside, Mowgli is found by Gray Brother, who brings news that Red Flower-singed Shere Khan has left to heal and vows to lay Mowgli's bones in the Waingunga; Mowgli reaffirms he will never forget he is a wolf despite his casting out.

scenes.title: Learning Men and Mocking Buldeo
scenes.summary: For three months Mowgli learns cloth, money, and plowing, angers children and priest, and at the fig-tree club openly mocks hunter Buldeo's ghost-tiger lies, earning appointment as buffalo herder.

scenes.title: Lazy Days Herding and Waiting
scenes.summary: Master of the buffalo herd, Mowgli leads lazy days at the wallows by the Waingunga, watching daily for Gray Brother's distant signal that Shere Khan has not yet returned.

scenes.title: News of Shere Khan and the Plan
scenes.summary: Gray Brother vanishes then reappears in the dhak ravine to warn that Shere Khan and Tabaqui have returned, and Mowgli devises a trap to catch the gorged tiger between divided buffalo herds.

scenes.title: Dividing the Herd
scenes.summary: Akela joins as wise helper and with Gray Brother neatly cuts cows and calves from bulls, driving them apart while Mowgli mounts Rama to begin the great circling movement.

scenes.title: Mowgli Springs the Trap
scenes.summary: Mowgli circles the bulls uphill to the head of the steep-sided ravine, rests them, and shouts down to wake Shere Khan and spring the trap.

scenes.title: The Buffalo Charge
scenes.summary: The bulls stampede down the ravine onto Shere Khan and crash into the cows below, killing the tiger, and Mowgli with Akela and Gray Brother scatters the maddened herds.

scenes.title: Skinning the Dead Tiger
scenes.summary: With Shere Khan dead beneath the buffalo trampling, Mowgli sets to skinning the ten-foot tiger alone for the Council Rock, slashing and tearing for an hour while the wolves tug as ordered.

scenes.title: Buldeo's Humbling
scenes.summary: Buldeo arrives demanding the hundred-rupee hide for Khanhiwara and threatens Mowgli with a beating, until Akela at Mowgli's word knocks him sprawling and Mowgli claims the skin as his own won in an old war.

scenes.title: Sorcerer Fear and the Finished Hide
scenes.summary: Terrified Buldeo begs release as from a sorcerer-king and flees to spread tales of magic, while Mowgli and the wolves finish drawing the great striped skin clear by twilight.

scenes.title: Stoned at the Village Gate
scenes.summary: Driving the buffaloes home at twilight, Mowgli is met at the village gate by stones, musket fire, and cries of sorcerer and wolf-demon. Bewildered, he confers with Akela, is warned by Messua that Buldeo calls him wizard and the crowd will kill him, bids her farewell, and orders Akela to drive the herd in through the crowd.

scenes.title: Farewell to the Children of Men
scenes.summary: After the herd scatters the crowd, Mowgli scornfully quits herding forever, spares the village for Messua's sake, and walks away with Akela under the stars to fetch Shere Khan's skin, while the horrified villagers watch him trot across the moonlit plain with wolves and embroider the tale.

scenes.title: Mowgli Spreads the Hide on the Council Rock
scenes.summary: By moonlight Mowgli brings Shere Khan's hide to Mother Wolf's cave and then to the Council Rock, where Bagheera joins him and Akela summons the remnant Pack to behold the trophy as Mowgli sings in triumph.

scenes.title: Mowgli Renounces the Pack Leadership
scenes.summary: Having kept his word, Mowgli refuses the Pack's plea to lead them, and with Bagheera's support declares he will hunt alone, joined only by his four wolf brothers.

scenes.title: Mowgli's Song
scenes.summary: The chapter closes with Mowgli's Song danced on the hide, recounting the kill, his casting out by both Packs, and his heavy-light heart torn between jungle and village.

scenes.title: Lullaby and Novastoshnah
scenes.summary: A seal lullaby opens into the narrator's framing tale from Limmershin the Winter Wren, introducing Novastoshnah on St. Paul Island as the great summer home of the seals.

scenes.title: The Crowded Fighting Beach
scenes.summary: The huge old bull Sea Catch fights for beach room among tens of thousands of roaring seals, then greets his wife Matkah; the crowded, foggy nursery beach is established.

scenes.title: A White Pup Learns the Sea
scenes.summary: Matkah's baby Kotick is born white to his parents' wonder; he learns playground games, his mother's swimming song, and to survive waves and the Killer Whale's fin.

scenes.title: Learning the Feel of the Water
scenes.summary: As the seals leave St. Paul's for winter, Matkah takes Kotick across the Pacific and teaches him to sleep on the swell and to feel bad weather tingling in his skin.

scenes.title: Following Wise Sea Pig
scenes.summary: Following the wise porpoise Sea Pig, Kotick learns to read gales and spends six months mastering deep-sea hunting, weather, and sea manners without touching land.

scenes.title: Spring Longing for Novastoshnah
scenes.summary: Lounging off Juan Fernandez, Kotick feels spring laziness and remembers Novastoshnah, then turns north for home, meeting scores of fellow holluschickie who greet him and marvel at his coat.

scenes.title: White Holluschickie Dances the Fire-Dance
scenes.summary: Now almost pure white and aching for land, Kotick returns to his birth beaches, dances the phosphorescent Fire-dance in the surf that night, then rolls in the new grass trading sea stories while older holluschickie tease the yearlings.

scenes.title: First Men Behind the Dune
scenes.summary: When asked about his white coat, Kotick says it grew, but is stopped short as Kerick Booterin and his son Patalamon appear from behind a dune to choose seals to drive to the killing-pens, his first sight of man.

scenes.title: The White Seal Ghost
scenes.summary: Patalamon spots the white seal and Kerick Booterin, terrified, takes him for old Zaharrof's ghost and warns not to touch or look at him, ordering the drove onward instead.

scenes.title: The Salt House Slaughter
scenes.summary: Kotick alone follows the driven holluschickie inland to the Salt House, where after cooling the drove, Kerick gives the order and men club the seals and rip off their skins.

scenes.title: Flight to Sea-Lion's Neck
scenes.summary: Horrified by the killing, Kotick gallops back to the sea and flings himself into the water at Sea-Lion's Neck, telling a gruff sea-lion that men are killing all the holluschickie.

scenes.title: The Counsel of the Sea-Lion
scenes.summary: The sea-lion tells Kotick seals will always be driven unless they can find an island where no men ever come, and advises him to rest and then swim to Walrus Islet to ask Sea Vitch; Kotick naps and heads for Walrus Islet.

scenes.title: Clam-Eater Cry
scenes.summary: Kotick lands at Walrus Islet by sleeping old Sea Vitch and wakes him. Mocked and told to run away when he asks for a men-free place for seals, he dolphin-jumps and shouts 'Clam-eater!', setting all the gulls screaming the insult till Sea Vitch rolls grunting.

scenes.title: Scorn at Novastoshnah
scenes.summary: Stung by the taunt, Sea Vitch tells Kotick to ask Sea Cow. Kotick swims back to Novastoshnah to find no sympathy for stopping the killing, not even from Sea Catch and Matkah, and goes off to dance the Fire-dance heavy-hearted.

scenes.title: Five Years Searching
scenes.summary: For five seasons Kotick searches the world's islands alone, finding only smoke or slaughter, until a dying last survivor of Masafuera tells of the prophecy of a white seal leader.

scenes.title: The Grazers off Copper Island
scenes.summary: Chasing halibut westward to Copper Island, Kotick sleeps on the swell and wakes on a weed bed to find huge, shovel-tailed, foolish-headed grazers bowing in the shoal water.

scenes.title: Finding Sea Cow at Last
scenes.summary: Kotick greets the split-lipped, bowing feeders, grows angry at their silence, then remembers the Burgomaster Gull and knows he has found the speechless Sea Cow at last.

scenes.title: Through the Tunnel to Safety
scenes.summary: Kotick patiently trails the slow herd north, follows their swift dive through a dark undersea tunnel, and surfaces to find perfect empty beaches safe from ships and men.

scenes.title: Kotick's Great Fight
scenes.summary: Laughed at on his return, Kotick accepts a young seal's challenge, defeats him, then in splendid rage charges the whole nursery, joined by his father Sea Catch until no seal dares resist.

scenes.title: The Exodus North
scenes.summary: The beaten seals pledge to follow Kotick to the Sea Cow's tunnel, and year by year more leave Novastoshnah and Lukannon for the safe northern beaches where Kotick reigns.

scenes.title: Lukannon Elegy
scenes.summary: The chapter closes with Lukannon, the sad deep-sea national anthem mourning the slaughtered beaches before the sealers came and pleading to the sea powers.

scenes.title: Dance with Death
scenes.summary: A martial song-chant frames the coming fight to the death between the mongoose and Nag, setting a foreboding, heroic tone.

scenes.title: Rescue and New Home
scenes.summary: Flood-washed Rikki-tikki is rescued, dried, and adopted by an English family; curious and fearless, he explores the bungalow and sleeps on Teddy's pillow despite the mother's fear of bites.

scenes.title: Sorrow in the Thorn-Bush
scenes.summary: Rikki-tikki explores the large garden hunting-ground and finds Darzee the tailorbird and his wife crying over their swaying nest in the thorn-bush.

scenes.title: Meeting Nag and Nagaina
scenes.summary: Rikki learns Nag ate Darzee's fledgling, confronts the risen cobra Nag, then leaps clear of a surprise strike from Nagaina behind him; both snakes retreat into the grass while Rikki withdraws to think.

scenes.title: Death of Karait
scenes.summary: Confident after his escape, Rikki dances and kills the deadly little Karait to save Teddy, then endures beating of the dead snake and the family's amazed fuss while he takes a dust-bath.

scenes.title: Night Whispers
scenes.summary: At night Rikki patrols the house, meets the fearful muskrat Chuchundra, and hears the faint scratch of snake scales on brickwork, realizing danger is inside the bathrooms.

scenes.title: The Snakes Plot Murder
scenes.summary: Rikki-tikki slips into the bathrooms and overhears Nag and Nagaina plotting outside to kill the family so the garden will be empty again for their hatching eggs. Nag enters through the bath-water sluice to wait and bite the big man in the morning. Rikki watches in fear as Nag drinks and coils asleep around the water-jar, creeping closer to choose where to strike.

scenes.title: Rikki Holds Death Grip
scenes.summary: Rikki-tikki decides he must seize Nag by the head above the hood and jumps, bracing against the jar. Nag thrashes him violently around the bathroom, but Rikki holds on with locked jaws. The awakened big man fires his shotgun into Nag behind the hood, killing him, and praises Rikki for saving their lives as the battered mongoose drags himself away.

scenes.title: News and a Plan
scenes.summary: Stiff but pleased next morning, Rikki finds Darzee triumphantly singing over Nag's corpse and angrily presses him to reveal where Nagaina keeps her eggs in the melon-bed to plan a decoy.

scenes.title: The Melon-Bed Eggs
scenes.summary: Darzee's sensible wife lures Nagaina away by feigning a broken wing while Rikki races to the melon-bed and crushes most of the twenty-five cobra eggs before being called to the house.

scenes.title: Hostage at Breakfast
scenes.summary: Rikki-tikki rushes to the veranda with the last cobra egg to find Nagaina coiled by Teddy's chair, holding Teddy and his parents stone-still with threats to strike. He taunts her to turn and fight, then shows her the egg to draw her eyes away from the boy.

scenes.title: The Last Egg and the Chase
scenes.summary: Rikki-tikki bargains over the last egg while Teddy's father drags Teddy safe, then mocks Nagaina and battles her across the veranda matting. Nagaina seizes the egg and flees for the thorn-bush, with Rikki-tikki following teeth-in-tail down into her dark rat-hole.

scenes.title: Victory and Rest
scenes.summary: Presumed dead, dirt-covered Rikki emerges victorious from the hole, sleeps through the afternoon, then is hailed garden-wide by the Coppersmith and tearfully thanked by the family as their guardian.

scenes.title: Darzee's Chaunt
scenes.summary: Darzee sings his formal chaunt in honor of ivory-fanged, red-eyed Rikki-tikki until Rikki interrupts and the rest of the song is lost.

scenes.title: Song of the Forest Longing
scenes.summary: Opening verse in Kala Nag's voice, yearning to break rope and chain and return to forest freedom, setting a wistful, wild mood.

scenes.title: The Black Snake's Forty-Seven Years
scenes.summary: Kala Nag the Black Snake is nearly seventy, with forty-seven years of Government service after being caught at twenty with his mother Radha Pyari. Taught not to fear, he became the best-loved elephant in India, carrying tents, guns, and mortars in Afghanistan, Abyssinia where he saw Emperor Theodore dead at Magdala, and at Ali Musjid, then hauling teak at Moulmein. Ten feet tall with shortened copper-bound tusks, he outworks any untrained elephant.

scenes.title: Tamer of Tuskers and Killer of Tigers
scenes.summary: Taken from timber work to catch wild elephants in the Garo hills, Kala Nag excels in the keddah. When wild herds are driven into the stockade, he enters the pandemonium by torchlight to hammer and subdue the largest tusker while others are roped. Wise in all fighting, he has faced charging wounded tigers alone, felling them with his own sickle-cut of the head and kneeling them to death.

scenes.title: Three Generations and the Black Snake
scenes.summary: Big Toomai boasts that Kala Nag fears only him after three generations of service, while Little Toomai claims the elephant fears him too and shows his intimate bond formed since birth, dreaming of future glory versus camp life.

scenes.title: The Boy Atop the Keddah Post
scenes.summary: During the torchlit driving into the Keddah stockade, Little Toomai climbs atop a quivering post and shouts encouragement to Kala Nag above the chaos, earning nods from the old catchers.

scenes.title: Meddling, a Slap, and a Scolding
scenes.summary: Little Toomai slips into the stockade to help rope a calf and is rescued by Kala Nag, earning a slap from his father and an angry morning scolding warning him against meddling and Petersen Sahib.

scenes.title: Petersen Sahib's Promise
scenes.summary: Pay-day gathering: Machua Appa praises the boy who threw the rope, Petersen Sahib lifts Little Toomai up, gives him four annas, and jokes he may enter the Keddah when he has seen the elephants dance.

scenes.title: Praise and Quarrel on the March
scenes.summary: Still happy at being noticed and rewarded by Petersen Sahib, Little Toomai asks about the elephant-dance while Big Toomai quarrels with an Assamese driver ahead whose new elephant is restless and hard to manage.

scenes.title: Talk of the Dance at the Ford
scenes.summary: The Assamese driver tells Little Toomai the wild elephants will dance now the drives are ended and warns to double-chain the pickets, which Big Toomai scorns as moonshine as they reach another ford of the Dihang.

scenes.title: Arrival at Camp and the Tom-Tom
scenes.summary: Wrangling and splashing through rivers, the line reaches the receiving-camp where the elephants are chained and fed, and in the evening Little Toomai borrows a tom-tom and drums happily alone before Kala Nag.

scenes.title: Shiv's Lullaby and Sleep by Kala Nag
scenes.summary: As the new elephants strain and trumpet at their ropes, Little Toomai's mother sings Shiv's lullaby to his small brother while Little Toomai keeps time on his drum until he falls asleep on the fodder by Kala Nag.

scenes.title: The Night Summons
scenes.summary: Moonlit silence broken by a wild elephant's call; the lines stir, Kala Nag snaps his grass string and slips away, taking Little Toomai up onto his neck into the forest.

scenes.title: Ride Through the Garo Forest
scenes.summary: A silent uphill drift then a crashing downhill rush through grass, river, and jungle trails, following fresh elephant tracks toward a trampled clearing.

scenes.title: The Elephant Dance
scenes.summary: Hidden ballroom crowded with scores of wild elephants of every age; after fearful waiting they stamp together for hours in the booming, earth-shaking dance.

scenes.title: Dawn and Return
scenes.summary: Dawn breaks and the herd vanishes, leaving enlarged trampled ground; exhausted and leg-weary, the boy rides with Pudmini back to camp and faints as he claims he saw the dance.

scenes.title: The Dance-Place Verified
scenes.summary: While Little Toomai sleeps, Petersen Sahib and Machua Appa follow the two elephants fifteen miles to the clearing, verify the trampled dance-place and seventy tracks crossing the river including Pudmini's leg-iron mark, marvel at what no man has seen, and return to camp where a feast is ordered.

scenes.title: Toomai of the Elephants
scenes.summary: Big Toomai returns as the camp feasts by the picketed elephants, the trackers honor Little Toomai as hero and mark his forehead with jungle-cock blood, and Machua Appa lifts him high proclaiming him Toomai of the Elephants while the whole tethered line raises trunks in trumpeting salute for his witnessing of the night dance.

scenes.title: Shiv and the Grasshopper
scenes.summary: Closing lullaby sung by Toomai's mother: Shiv allots food to all creatures while Parbati hides a grasshopper, proving even the least is provided for.

scenes.title: Rainy Camp Stampede
scenes.summary: Opening verse gives way to a rain-soaked review camp at Rawal Pindi. Loose camels stampede in the dark and collapse the narrator's tent, forcing him to flee into the mud.

scenes.title: Shelter Among the Guns
scenes.summary: The narrator stumbles to the artillery lines and shelters under guns in the drizzle. A screw-gun mule passes jingling in the dark.

scenes.title: Camel's Complaint
scenes.summary: A lost baggage-camel confesses he fought the narrator's tent. Old mule Billy scolds him for disturbing the camp and kicks him to sit down.

scenes.title: Troop-Horse Arrives
scenes.summary: Cavalry troop-horse Number Fifteen joins them, complaining of broken sleep. The camel pleads bad dreams while Billy warns the gun-bullocks are coming.

scenes.title: Bullocks and Recruit
scenes.summary: Yoked siege-gun bullocks and a terrified young battery-mule arrive. The recruit whimpers about fearful Things in the lines and clings to Billy.

scenes.title: First Fears
scenes.summary: The veterans reassure the recruit with first-fright stories of men, harness, and kicking. The young mule insists his Things were like falling, bubbling trees.

scenes.title: Bridle-Wise and Mountain Science
scenes.summary: Talk turns to active service. The troop-horse explains bridle-wisdom and charging with Dick Cunliffe, while Billy defends sure-footed mountain obedience.

scenes.title: Knives, Ledges, and Squares
scenes.summary: The horse describes facing knives and trusting his rider; Billy praises hidden mountain ledges and poppy shells below. The camel timidly offers his own seated-square way of fighting.

scenes.title: One Way of Fighting
scenes.summary: The twin bullocks preach pulling the big gun when Two Tails trumpets as Fate. Billy mocks them, then he and the horse erupt into a furious pedigree quarrel, Brumby versus jackass.

scenes.title: Two Tails Interrupts
scenes.summary: A deep elephant voice stops the rearing fight. Both horse and mule subside in disgust as Two Tails announces he is picketed and has overheard them.

scenes.title: The Elephant's Fear
scenes.summary: Two Tails explains being betwixt and between, seeing shells burst inside his head and distrusting his driver. Bullocks, horse, and mule debate blood, bravery, and seeing out versus seeing in.

scenes.title: Trumpet and Terrier
scenes.summary: Two Tails trumpets to prove fear, shaking horse and mule. Little dog Vixen finds the narrator and bullies the terrified elephant around his pickets.

scenes.title: Hukm Hai - Obey
scenes.summary: Calm returns with talk of different fears. The recruit asks why they fight at all, and all answer as one: Hukm hai, obey the man at your head without questions.

scenes.title: White Man Panic
scenes.summary: The bullocks prepare to leave unafraid, then learn a white man hides under the gun. Panicking because white men eat beef, they snap their yoke escaping in the mud.

scenes.title: Biscuits and Good Nights
scenes.summary: The narrator reflects on cattle fearing beef-eaters. Billy marches the recruit back to lines, while the troop-horse nuzzles for biscuits and arranges parade places with boastful Vixen.

scenes.title: The March Past and the Advancing Wall
scenes.summary: In sunshine then rain, infantry, cavalry, elephants hauling a siege-gun, oxen and screw-guns march past, then form a vast advancing wall that shakes the ground and startles the Amir until it halts and salutes.

scenes.title: There Was an Order and They Obeyed
scenes.summary: As the troops leave in the rain, a Central Asian chief asks how the wonder was done, and a native officer explains the chain of obedience from beast and driver up through sergeant to Viceroy, servant of the Empress.

scenes.title: Parade-Song of the Camp Animals
scenes.summary: The camp animals' parade-song sounds each arm's voice, from ten-foot elephant teams to bullocks, cavalry canter, climbing mules and grumbling camels, united as children of the camp.
